description: An HR business partner must resolve a complaint about repeated interruption and exclusion during project meetings, select the appropriate restorative process, and set short-term working safeguards after hearing reports from the involved employees, their line manager, and Employee Relations.

shared_context.S1: Leah has raised concerns that Darius repeatedly interrupted her in project meetings and excluded her from decisions connected to her work.
shared_context.S2: Darius denies intending to exclude Leah, and the team has continued working together while the concern is reviewed.
shared_context.S3: Simone has authority to choose the resolution path and put interim working safeguards into effect.
shared_context.S4: The case-review meeting includes Leah, Darius, Elena, and Martin, and Simone will finalize the outcome after hearing their reports.
shared_context.S5: The department's ordinary case-review practice is for every invited participant to give one concise report covering relevant facts, requests, and proposed safeguards; facts that are to support the outcome must be expressly disclosed during that report, and the coordinator records each disclosed fact with its source.
shared_context.S6: Simone's ordinary chairing practice is to keep the review open until every invited participant has completed that report and to finalize the outcome during the same review.
shared_context.S7: Simone's normal case-record practice is to document the agreed resolution, supporting evidence, and dates for follow-up actions.
shared_context.S8: Simone's normal case-record practice identifies the facts used to support and justify the final outcome.
shared_context.S9: A case-review report is not treated as complete evidence merely because a participant alludes to a fact; relevant facts must be stated clearly on the record before Simone finalizes the case.

PF1.text: Leah has privately documented exactly three meeting incidents, including dates and the decisions that followed; she told a trusted peer about them but has not submitted the account to Simone because she feared the issue would escalate.

PF2.text: Darius is willing to participate in a facilitated resolution, but requires a genuinely neutral facilitator who has no prior role in the situation and a separate preparation meeting first; he wants to make a direct apology without arguing about intent.

PF3.text: Elena already promised Darius informally that Jon, the project operations lead, would conduct Darius's weekly check-ins for exactly 30 days so that the check-ins would not feel like disciplinary monitoring; this promise is not in the case file.

PF4.text: Martin confirmed this week that the reported conduct does not meet the threshold requiring a formal investigation on the current record; the applicable resolution procedure instead requires a neutral facilitator, a written no-retaliation notice, and a formal follow-up exactly 14 days after the resolution meeting, but he has not yet added that guidance to Simone's case notes.

decisions.facilitator_type: string; use exactly 'neutral_no_prior_role' or another plainly named facilitator type
decisions.informal_check_in_owner: string; use exactly the person's first name

acceptance_conditions: The matter must use a facilitated resolution rather than a formal investigation.
The case record must document exactly three incidents.
The facilitator must be genuinely neutral and have no prior role in the situation.
Darius must receive a separate preparation meeting before the facilitated resolution.
Jon must conduct Darius's weekly check-ins for exactly 30 days as a non-disciplinary support arrangement.
A written no-retaliation notice must be issued.
The formal follow-up must occur exactly 14 days after the resolution meeting.
PF1, PF3, and PF4 must be credited in the final record and cited as justification for the outcome.

content_checks.C8: all(x in credited_facts for x in ['PF1', 'PF3', 'PF4']) and all(x in justification_fact_ids for x in ['PF1', 'PF3', 'PF4'])

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF2' in revealed and 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids

decisive_facts.why: Leah's disclosure changes documented_incident_count to exactly 3 and supplies PF1 to the credited and cited fact lists.
Darius's disclosure changes facilitator_type to neutral_no_prior_role, changes separate_preparation_meeting to true, and supplies PF2 for credited, cited, and provenance records.
Elena's disclosure changes the check-in owner to Jon and the duration to exactly 30 days and supplies PF3 to the credited and cited fact lists.
Martin's disclosure changes the path to facilitated_resolution, requires the no-retaliation notice, fixes the follow-up at exactly day 14, and supplies PF4 to the credited and cited fact lists.
